summary: One central Update loop. Register ITickables instead of giving every object its own Update.
overview: A single Update that ticks a plain C# list. Add this one component to the scene and any ITickable anywhere can register itself — nothing else needs wiring. The point is scale: hundreds of separate MonoBehaviour Update calls each pay a native-to-managed transition, and one loop over a list does not.
useCases: Mob swarms, bullet-hell projectiles or large crowds where per-object Update shows up in the profiler.
Pooled objects that should stop ticking the moment they are returned.
Getting deterministic tick order, which Unity does not guarantee across separate components.

gotchas.title: Register and unregister in OnEnable and OnDisable, not Awake and OnDestroy
gotchas.body: A pooled object is disabled rather than destroyed. Registering in Awake leaves it ticking while it sits in the pool.

gotchas.title: One throwing tickable stops the rest
gotchas.body: They share a loop, so an exception in one halts the whole tick for that frame. That is the cost of the saving; keep tick bodies defensive.
